utena: [Yādicchakanāma]  CL=8 King named Utena (Udena). He was the son of King Parantapa of Kosambi. When his mother was pregnant, a giant bird carried her away thinking she was meat and placed her on a banyan tree in Himavanta, where she gave birth. He was named Utena because he was born taking the essence of rain, mountain, and dawn. Utena and his mother were cared for by the hermit Allakappa. When King Parantapa passed away, the hermit Allakappa taught Utena mantras to summon and control elephants, then sent him to Kosambi to become king. See also: Udena.

[Yādicchakanāma]  CL=8 About the person named Uttiya: Uttiya Thera was the son of a brahmin in Savatthi. When he came of age, he became a wandering ascetic (paribbājaka) searching for the deathless state (amata dhamma). He approached the Buddha, listened to the Dhamma, and then ordained as a monk in the Buddha"s dispensation.
Because he did not properly purify his moral conduct (sīla) and other practices, he could not attain higher spiritual attainments. When he asked the Buddha for guidance, the Buddha advised him saying 'Therefore Uttiya, purify yourself from the very beginning' (Tasmātiha tvaṃ Uttiya ādimeva visodhehi).

utugāhāpanattha: [Utu+gāhāpana+attha]  CL=7 The benefit of causing to take or experience the weather (such as hot or cold).
utuja: [Utu+jana+kvi]  CL=7 That which arises due to the weather (such as hot and cold).
utujarūpa: [Utuja+rūpa]  CL=7 The physical form that arises due to the weather (such as cold and hot).
utukakkhaḷatā: [Utu+kakkhaḷatā]  CL=7 The state of extreme weather (such as hot or cold).
utukkhāna: [Utu+akkhāna]  CL=7 To formally ask about the weather (such as the seasons; Winter, Rainy Season, and Hot Season)
utukāla: [Utu+kāla]  CL=7 (1) The periods of winter and summer. (2) The time when a woman experiences the menstrual cycle.
utumattakkha: [Utu+manda+akkhi]  CL=7 One whose eyes are dim due to the hot season.
utumatī: [Utu+mantu+ī]  CL=7 A woman who experiences the menstrual cycle.
utumaya: [Utu+maya]  CL=7 That which arises due to the season.
utunikāla: [Utunī+kāla]  CL=7 A period when a woman experiences the menstrual cycle.
utuniyāma: [Utu+niyāma]  CL=7 The firm characteristics of seasons.
utunī: [Utu+inī]  CL=7 A woman is experiencing the menstrual cycle.
utupaccaya: [Utu+paccaya]  CL=7 A cause that is the season.
utupaccayautusamuṭṭhāna: [Utupaccaya+utu+samuṭṭhāna]  CL=8 That which has season/temperature as its cause, produced by season/temperature; that which has the previous season/temperature as its cause, produced by the subsequent season/temperature.
utupaccayaāhārasamuṭṭhāna: [Utupaccaya+āhāra+samuṭṭhāna]  CL=7 That which arises due to nutrients has a cause that is the season (such as hot or cold).
utuparissaya: [Utu+parissaya]  CL=7 (1) The season that afflicts. (2) The danger or harm that is the season. See - Utuparissayavinodana.
utuparissayavinodana: [Utuparissaya+vinodana]  CL=7 (1) Warding off the perils of seasonal weather. (2) Warding off the seasonal weather and danger or harm.
utuparissayavinodanattha:
[Utuparissayavinodana+attha]  CL=8 1. The benefit of dispelling/removing dangers related to weather/seasons
2. The benefit of dispelling/removing weather/seasonal hazards and dangers
utupariṇāma: [Utu+pariṇāma]  CL=7 The transformation of the seasonal weather. The different nature of seasonal weather. See also - Ubhupariṇāmaja, utupariṇāmana.
utupariṇāmaja: [Utupariṇāma+jana+kvi]  CL=8 That which arises due to the transformation/alteration of the seasons/weather, that which arises due to discordant/incompatible weather conditions different from the previous season.
utupariṇāmana: [Utu+pariṇāmana]  CL=7 The transformation of the seasonal weather.
utupariṇāmī: [Utupariṇāma+ī]  CL=7 Having the transformation of the seasonal weather or development in due season.
utupharaṇasadisa: [Utupharaṇa+sadisa]  CL=7 Resembling the diffusion of the radiated heat.
utupharaṇattha: [Utu+pharaṇattha]  CL=7 The benefit of showing or teaching the diffusion of heat.
utupharaṇaṭṭhāniya: [Utupharaṇa+ṭhāniya]  CL=7 Standing in the diffusion of heat.
utuppamāṇācikkhana: [Utuppamāṇa+ācikkhana]  CL=7 Speaking or teaching about the measurement of weather.
utupubba: [Utu+pubba]  CL=7 (The festival) that celebrates in the beginning of that season in the six seasons.
utupuṇṇatā: [Utu+puṇṇa+tā]  CL=7 The state of the fullness of the monsoon.
utusamatā: [Utu+samatā]  CL=7 The equilibrium state of the seasons.
utusamaya:
[Utu+samaya]  CL=7 1. The time when the season/weather arrives
2. The seasonal time (referring to winter, summer, and rainy seasons)
utusamaññā: [Utu+samaññā]  CL=7 The name of the season.
utusampadā: [Utu+sampadā]  CL=7 The completenss or fulfillment of the season.
utusampanna: [Utu+sampanna]  CL=7 Completed with the temperate season (neither too hot nor too cold).'
utusampupphita: [Utu+saṃpupphita(sampupphita)]  CL=7 Blossomed during the (spring, summer, and rainy seasons).
utusamuṭṭhāna: [Utu+samuṭṭhāna]  CL=7 That which arises due to the seasonal weather.
utusamuṭṭhānarūpasamudāya: [Utusamuṭṭhāna+rūpasamudāya]  CL=7 A group of physical forms that arise due to the seasonal weather.
utusamuṭṭhānarūpasantati: [Utusamuṭṭhāna+rūpasantati]  CL=7 The sequence of physical forms that arise due to the seasonal weather.
utusamuṭṭhānasītuṇhavāta: [Utusamuṭṭhāna+sītuṇhavāta]  CL=7 The cold wind and the hot wind that arise due to seasonal changes.
utusamuṭṭhānika: [Utusamuṭṭhāna+ika]  CL=7 Having a cause due to the seasonal weather.
utusamuṭṭhānikakāya: [Utusamuṭṭhānika+kāya]  CL=7 A group of the physical forms that arise due to the seasonal weather.
utusamuṭṭhānikapaṭibandhaka: [Utusamuṭṭhānika+paṭibandhaka]  CL=6 That which is linked or connected with the sequence of the physical forms that arise due to the seasonal weather.
utusamuṭṭhānikarūpakalāpa: [Utusamuṭṭhānika+rūpakalāpa]  CL=7 A group of forms that arise due to seasonal weather.
utusappāya: [Utu+sappāya]  CL=7 An agreeable season or that which is appropriate by the power of a temperate season.
utusappāyalābha: [Utusappāya+lābha]  CL=7 Getting the appropriate weather or temperate weather.
utusappāyasiddha: [Utusappāya+siddha]  CL=7 That which is finised by the temperate season.
utusappāyaṭṭhāna: [Utusappāya+ṭhāna]  CL=7 A place where there is temperate weather.
utusaṃpupphita: [Utu+saṃpupphita(sampupphita)]  CL=7 Blossomed during (winter, summer, and rainy season).
utusukha:
[Utu+sukha]  CL=8 Translation:
1. (a) Comfort/wellbeing that depends on or arises from weather/seasons
(b) Weather that brings comfort/wellbeing
(c) (adjective form)
2. (a) Having comfort that depends on seasonal conditions
(b) Having weather that brings comfort
utusukhasamphassa: [Utusukha+samphassa]  CL=7 Experiencing pleasant sensations influenced by the season.
utusukhasevanatā: [Utusukha+sevanatā]  CL=7 A person who experiences the temperate season that brings comfort.
ututtaya: [Utu+taya]  CL=7 A group of three seasons (winter, summer, and rainy season). See-Ututtayānurūpatā.
ututtayānurūpatā: [Ututtaya+anurūpatā]  CL=7 That which is suitable for all three seasons (winter, summer, and rainy season).
utuvaṭṭa: [Utu+vaṭṭa]  CL=7 The winter and rainy season. See-Utuvassa.
utuveramaṇī: [Utu+veramaṇī]  CL=7 A woman who does not experience menstruation.
utuvikāra: [Utu+vikāra]  CL=7 The transformation of the season.
utuvipariṇāma: [Utu+vipariṇāma]  CL=7 The transformation of the season.
utuvipariṇāmaja: [Utuvipariṇāma+jana+kvī]  CL=7 That which arises due to the transformation of season.
utuvisabhāga: [Utu+visabhāga]  CL=7 The different nature of the seasons.
utuvāra: [Utu+vāra]  CL=7 An occasion of the occurrence the season (winter, summer, and rainy season).
utuācikkhana: [Utu+ācikkhana]  CL=7 To famally ask about the season.
utuāhāraja: [Utu+āhāra+jana+kvi]  CL=7 That which arises due to season and nutrients.
utuāhārajarūpa: [Utuāhāraja+rūpa]  CL=7 A form that arises due to season and nutrients.
uttaritu: [U+tara+tuṃ]  CL=7 (A) to crossover. (2) To overcome. (3) To rise up.
uttasa: [U+tasi+a]  CL=7 [Uddhaṃ tasīyateti uttaṃso. Dhāna,ṭī.3va8] (1) Earrings. (2) Head ornaments.
uttānikaroti: [Uttāna+karoti]  CL=7 Makes to be clear or self-evident. See also - Uttānīkaroti.
uttānīkātu: [Uttāna+kātuṃ]  CL=7 To clarify what is evident.
uttāretu: [U+tara+ṇe+tuṃ]  CL=7 (A) To take out. (B) To overcome.
utusapupphita: [Utu+saṃpupphita(sampupphita)]  CL=7 Blossomed during (winter, summer, and rainy season).
